neighbours.label: the token ' late' in the idiom 'too late' (missed chance); plain temporal 'late' and other 'too X' stay quiet
fire: By the time the ambulance came, it was too late.
She called back, but it was already too late.
It's too late to cancel the order now.
We got there too late to see the opening act.
Is it too late to apply for the scholarship?
The warning came too late for the villagers.
I tried to stop him, but I was too late.
It was too late to fix the mistake before printing.
quiet: By the time the ambulance came, it was the late shift.
She called back late in the evening.
It's too soon to cancel the order now.
We got there late and missed the opening act.
Is it too hard to apply for the scholarship?
The warning came in late spring for the villagers.
I tried to stop him, but I was too slow.
It was too difficult to fix the mistake before printing.
neighbours.notes: Peaks on ' late' after 'too' (27 of top 32 peaks). Weaker after other degree words ('a little late for that' 0.41, 'so late that' 0.29), so near misses avoid degree+late. Missed-chance meaning without the word is silent (0.00). Partial cross-lingual: 'demasiado tarde' 0.27. Inverse solver (differential evolution) found no leak. Label chosen by Twitch chat vote (default option, no votes cast).
